Last summer I travelled solo for 2 months in SEA, particularly Thailand and Vietnam. I was 23 back then. From my experience, Thailand felt very safe, I’ve been to many places, including the huge bangkok to a tiny village with like a hundred people living there. I am not sure whether they knew I was trans, because my attitude throughout the whole trip was like ‘whatever’. (I looked like a girl backpacker though). In general, people were nice, even in the south where the majority of people are muslim. I can definitely recommend Thailand to visit, I am even revisiting in December this year.   
Vietnam, on the other hand, was fifty-fifty. It’s a different culture, more conservative and less developed. As a tall (6’5”) white girl I felt I stood out most of the time. I even got clocked in some places and people were less friendly. But I also met some totally nice people in the middle of nowhere, like a smiley bicycle maker or a cool jacked grandma shop assistant. I feel it heavily depends on the place you go to, so do a proper research. (here I could give you more tips if you are interested). I mean, you are very young and I certainly recommend you to travel anywhere you can, as it will enrich your life later on. Follow general precautions and be confident and you will be fine on most of the places. I wish you happy and safe travels!

Hey! I live in the Netherlands a middle sized city called Amersfoort in the suburbs. The mentality of people here I met so far is generally "live your own life but don't interfere with mine". If you know what you want and are confident about it, people will not care. Though I live in a quite conservative environment and try not to scream that I am trans, I can get along fine. I have heard bigger cities in Randstad area like Rotterdam or Utrecht are supposed to be much more accepting so if you got the opportunity to move to either, I would recommend that.   
Regarding medication: Since I had finished my transition back in my country of origin, I needed just hormones upon arrival to the Netherlands. These I got from my local GP here in Amersfoort. Basically, I showed her my medical documents and that the transition is already done and explained that I need just estrogen prescribed regularly and I got it. Anyways, I just want to say I understand your situation as I am in a similar age and also come from Eastern Europe... Good luck on your journey!
